title: Bands Leonce played with; the Christian swap
summary: Leonce also worked with other bands, and Mello recalls a swap involving Charlie Christian and a disagreement with Jack Laine.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Did Lyle's work with many bands that you didn't work with? Well,

he worked with Galatay. He worked with Christian. He worked with Baraka. And he worked with Monjada, Triangle Officer. Which Monjada's in it? Sato. Sam. The clarinet player? I believe it is. And which Christian? Frank Christian played cornet. And Beans Christian, Emil, he played cornet. And who else did the horse play? He lost the horse to somebody else. His main hole after he left us was to play with Frank Christian. We made a swap. I took Charlie and he went over to play. Plus he had some kind of disagreement with Jack Lane. It used to be. It was a pretty good swap when I took Charlie over and he told me that I was going to have two tubas in the band. I told the fellow that told me that and he was supposed to be a good friend of mine and he ain't no friend of mine. I found out to be a double crosser. I says, well, I'd soon have two tubas and two cornets. He says, you know what you're talking about. I said, maybe I don't because Charlie Christian played everything in the bass clap. Charlie couldn't play in treble clef to save his cell or slide from home. He'd play like that on a horn. On that horn he had, man, when he'd get half drunk and him and Jack Lane get all the pickups, drop all the drugs and he'd out on the floor. I never seen Martin Abraham for a long time. Anybody, you ever seen Martin Abraham lately? I haven't seen him lately. Have you, Paul? Just in March. First of March, I guess, was the last time I saw him. Is he playing in town? Just some spots, I think. I think he made, he might have made a record with Raymond, Burke, not too long ago. I'm not sure.
